record.paper_title: Higher Rank Brill-Noether Theory and Coherent Systems: Open Questions
record.original_question: To what extent do Brill-Noether loci and moduli spaces of coherent systems determine the underlying curve C; in other words, what Torelli-type statements hold for these moduli spaces?

evidence.quote: Question 9.4. To what extent do Brill-Noether loci and moduli spaces of coherent systems determine the curve C?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $C$ be a smooth irreducible projective curve of genus $g \geq 2$ over the complex numbers. For integers $n \geq 1$, $d$, and $k \geq 1$, recall the following moduli-theoretic objects associated to $C$:

(a) The Brill–Noether locus $B^{k}_{n,d}(C) \subset M_{n,d}(C)$ inside the moduli space $M_{n,d}(C)$ of (semi)stable vector bundles of rank $n$ and degree $d$ on $C$, defined as the locus of bundles $E$ with $h^{0}(C,E) \geq k$.

(b) The moduli space $G(\alpha; n,d,k)$ of $\alpha$-(semi)stable coherent systems $(E,V)$ of type $(n,d,k)$ on $C$, where $E$ is a vector bundle of rank $n$ and degree $d$ on $C$, $V \subseteq H^{0}(C,E)$ is a linear subspace of dimension $k$, and $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}_{>0}$ is a stability parameter.

Formulate and resolve Torelli-type statements for these moduli spaces. Specifically: determine the extent to which the isomorphism class of $C$ is recovered from the data of one (or several) of the moduli spaces $B^{k}_{n,d}(C)$ or $G(\alpha;n,d,k)(C)$, as an abstract variety. That is, identify ranges of parameters $(n,d,k,\alpha)$ for which an isomorphism
$$B^{k}_{n,d}(C) \cong B^{k}_{n,d}(C') \quad \text{or} \quad G(\alpha;n,d,k)(C) \cong G(\alpha;n,d,k)(C')$$
of complex varieties implies $C \cong C'$, and conversely characterize cases where the moduli space fails to determine $C$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open research direction in higher-rank Brill–Noether theory. While classical Torelli theorems are known for moduli of stable bundles (Mumford–Newstead, Narasimhan–Ramanan, Kouvidakis–Pantev) and partial Torelli-type results exist for some Brill–Noether loci, a comprehensive answer covering the full range of Brill–Noether loci and coherent system moduli spaces does not appear in the literature. No source found resolves this in general.

status_evidence.title: Coherent Systems and Brill–Noether Theory
status_evidence.snippet: Coherent systems provide partial desingularizations of Brill-Noether loci, used to study their geometry.
status_evidence.claim: Coherent systems are tools to study Brill-Noether loci geometry, but Torelli-type reconstructions are not addressed in general.
